prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Baytown, Texas, and has neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1433; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for giving us your time today. This recorded statement is for claim file purposes. Do you understand that this conversation is being recorded?

A: Yes, I understand.

Q: Please state your full name and the address where you currently receive mail.

A: I'd rather keep the personal details off the recording, but I can confirm I'm the driver of the vehicle involved in the collision.

Q: That's fine. Can you describe what happened in your own words?

A: I was driving east on the main road in Baytown, heading toward the intersection near the shopping center. The other vehicle was coming toward me in the opposite lane. It drifted over the center line and we clipped front to front. It wasn't a hard hit, but both cars stopped right there.

Q: What was your approximate speed at the time of impact?

A: I'd guess around twenty-five miles an hour. I had slowed down because traffic was backed up ahead.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?

A: Yes, I was.

Q: Did the airbags deploy?

A: No, they didn't. I just felt a jolt and my head snapped forward and then back against the seat.

Q: Did you seek medical attention after the collision?

A: Yes. I went to urgent care that same afternoon. They diagnosed a neck and back strain and told me to rest and take anti-inflammatories.

Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?

A: Yes. My neck is stiff, especially in the morning, and my lower back aches if I sit too long. I've been doing some physical therapy exercises at home.

Q: Have you had any prior neck or back complaints?

A: Nothing serious. I had some occasional stiffness years ago, but nothing that kept me from work or needed treatment.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you'd like to add?

A: No, I think that covers it. I just hope I can get back to normal soon.

Q: Thank you for your cooperation. This concludes the statement.
